markdown_report:
The best next experiment is a frozen SASRec with a scale-calibrated recent-history residual, selected exclusively by the pinned macro validation HR@10. At 10% research progress, this provides a feasible test of the starting hypothesis.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Freezing SASRec isolates the residual’s immediate contribution. A zero coefficient preserves baseline scores. (2) Recent-history similarity could strengthen specific interests identified in the qualitative diagnosis. It could also amplify substitutes, so improvement remains uncertain. (3) Pairwise margins depend on score scale. Residual calibration and paired ranking comparisons are therefore more informative than raw margin changes alone.

**Insights from supplied related work.** (1) The [recency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) motivates testing excessive recent-item emphasis. It does not establish the correct recency strength for these categories. (2) [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows that sampled and full-catalog rankings can disagree. Simulator feedback therefore supplements the pinned objective. (3) The supplied [complementary-reranking paper](https://genai-personalization.github.io/assets/papers/GenAIRecP2025/5_Xu.pdf) motivates distinguishing similarity from functional relationships. Titles alone cannot establish compatibility or an unmet need.

Three directions follow: calibrate recency, diagnose sensitivity, and audit relationship evidence.

| Direction | Existing signal | Proposed extension | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recency | SASRec contextual scores | Frozen cosine residual | Useful horizon varies |
| Sensitivity | Training-pair margins | Residual-off paired comparisons | Generalization remains unproven |
| Relationships | Titles/descriptions | Evidence-backed overlap flags | Actual needs are unobserved |

Three candidate ideas are assessed below; difficulty increases with score. Each assessment gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibrated recent residual | 3: controlled combination; familiar components | 7: cheap hypothesis test; may reinforce redundancy | 2: scoring-only addition; adapter consistency required |
| History-coherence gate | 5: adaptive residual; heuristic gate | 6: varies recency by history; coherence may misrepresent intent | 4: simple statistics; extra tuning |
| Text-supported overlap penalty | 5: evidence-grounded reranking; established approach | 6: addresses overlap; repetition can be desirable | 6: no pretrained weights needed; lexical rules are brittle |

**Selected algorithm.** Normalize frozen item embeddings, average the latest K nonpadding embeddings at each prefix, and normalize that average. Score candidates with SASRec plus α times calibrated cosine similarity. Estimate calibration once from training-pair margin standard deviations. Compare baseline with K∈{3,10} and α∈{0.05,0.10,0.20}; retain baseline unless validation improves.

Preserve all four routes, seeds, splits, DATA_DIR, and predictor serialization. Expose residual-off scoring to DiagnosisProbe and keep aligned prefix features. Report paired category gains/losses and macro differences; training diagnostics and twenty-user qualitative feedback are descriptive evidence, not substitutes for validation.

idea.description: Freeze each category’s SASRec and add a candidate-independent, scale-calibrated cosine residual from the most recent K interactions. Include the unchanged baseline in validation selection.
idea.motivation: The diagnosis suggests that broad relevance sometimes overwhelms recent specific interests. A small residual tests whether emphasizing those interests improves the fixed benchmark, while acknowledging that similarity may also increase redundant recommendations.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all category routes, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Train the baseline once per category within the shared budget, then freeze it. Compute calibration only from public training pairs in evaluation mode. Use one shared K and alpha configuration across categories, selected by macro validation HR@10; break ties in favor of alpha=0. Save the baseline checkpoint, K, alpha, and category-specific calibration beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct identical scoring. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. The compatibility view can return concatenated SASRec and recent-history features of shape B×L×2D; predict_score must handle this layout and expose predict_score_base. Preserve view.model as the actual deployed nn.Module and retain item_emb, user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Mark unavailable metadata and simulator traits explicitly unavailable. No executable replacement train.py is specified here because the supplied input contains no baseline implementation or predictor interface.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Train SASRec using the existing pipeline; freeze parameters and enter eval mode.
  E[i] = normalize(item_embedding[i]); keep padding embedding zero.
  For K in {3, 10}:
    At every prefix t, r[t] = normalize(mean(E[last K nonpadding items through t])).
    On fixed training pairs, collect base margins db and cosine margins dc.
    scale[K] = std(db) / std(dc) when std(dc) > epsilon; otherwise 0.
    score(t, i; alpha, K) = base_score(t, i) + alpha * scale[K] * dot(r[t], E[i]).
Compare baseline and six shared (K, alpha) configurations with alpha in {0.05, 0.10, 0.20}, using identical pinned validation users and candidates.
Select highest four-category macro HR@10; prefer baseline on ties.
Serialize selected settings and write the matching predictor.
Run residual-on/off diagnostics on identical training pairs; report them separately from validation.

originality.positive: Combines frozen sequential scores with explicit scale calibration and a directly measurable residual ablation.
originality.negative: Recent-history pooling and additive similarity scoring are established techniques; novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for testing adaptive horizons and history-dependent residual strengths.
future_potential.negative: A cosine residual cannot identify compatibility, fulfilled needs, or whether repeated interests imply another purchase.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no additional encoder training, external data, or downloaded weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Prefix alignment, calibration, diagnostic hooks, and exported predictor scoring must agree exactly.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: The supplied summary motivates measuring excessive emphasis on recent interactions.
limitations: Does not establish the useful residual strength or history horizon for this task.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled evaluation can disagree with full-catalog evaluation, including model-order reversals.
limitations: Does not determine which model improves the pinned benchmark; direct validation remains necessary.

related_work.title: LLM-enhanced complementary reranking paper
contributions: The supplied summary motivates distinguishing complementary relationships from broad similarity.
limitations: Textual relationship judgments do not verify compatibility or user needs.
Its LLM-based approach is not required for the selected embedding-only experiment.
